description.text: By default, flares will be as wide as they are high. This value can be manipulated to simulate an anamorphic lens.

This slider determines the angle of the asymmetry.

Depending on the simulated lens, this value can be linked to the overall flare angle.
rel
Curve shape of the falloff.
Makes sections of the flare darker.
Number of repeats around the circumference of the flare.
Changes the overall brightness of the flare.
The chroma shift moves color components in the direction set below.
This slider determines the angle of the chroma shift. Depending on the simulated lens, this value can be linked to the overall flare angle.
rel

The chroma spread moves color components to and from the center of the flare. Positive values shift red outward and blue inward. Large spreads will create a red/green/blue banding instead of a rainbow like effect. This can be compensated for by changing the color falloffs.
rel
Some physical lens flares appear flattened on their sides. The Flare operator can simulate polygonal shapes with 3 or more corners.
Changes the angular position of the first corner in a polygonal flare. Depending on the simulated lens, this value can be linked to the overall flare angle.
This knob controls the amount of flattening of the flare's sides. A value of 0 create a circular flare, 1 will render a polygon with straight edges and sharp corners.

Flares fade from black at the outer radius to the 'ring color' on the middle radius to the 'inner color' on the inner radius. The overall brightness of the flare can be set in the 'visibility' section.
The inner falloff describes the way in which the ring color blends into inner background color. The falloff can be set for each color component independently.
...brightness
...hue
...edge flattening

Create multiple flares with similar settings.

If more than one flare is requested, all of them will be randomized according to the parameters below.

The appearance of multiple flares can be changed by choosing a different master seed, or by choosing different seed on individual settings below. To 'tie' two amounts together, give them the same seed.
Random variance of the flare position along the lightsource/center line.
...rotation

Create multiple flares with similar settings.

If more than one flare is requested, all of them will be randomized according to the parameters below.

The appearance of multiple flares can be changed by choosing a different master seed, or by choosing different seed on individual settings below. To 'tie' two amounts together, give them the same seed.
...size
...visibility
The 'offset' moves the flare along an invisible line between the center of the screen (0) and the light source (1).
The outer falloff describes the way in which the ring color blends into the image background color. The falloff can be set for each color component independently.

This knobs holds the center position of the flare. The flare can be repositioned along an imaginary line between 'position' and the center of the format by changing the 'offset' below. This is helpful to simulate multiple flares in a lens flare. In this case, 'position' should hold the position of the light source.

The size of a flare is calculated using three radii. A flare is similar to a very flexible donut shape. The inner radius describes the size of the 'hole' and fills with the 'inner color'. The thickest part of the donut is the 'middle radius' and fills with the 'ring color'. Nothing will be drawn outside the 'outer radius'.

Flares fade from black at the outer radius to the 'ring color' on the middle radius to the 'inner color' on the inner radius. The overall brightness of the flare can be set in the 'visibility' section.
Use this control to lower the sharpness of corners created by the 'flattening' slider.
Multiply the global size of the flare while keeping the ratio between the radii.
Set this knob to values greater 0 to speed up the flare rendering by sacrificing horizontal resolution. A value of 0 renders at full resolution.
Set the relative distance of the lightsource to the matte box, at which the flare will be fully visible.
The value of the vis mask will be multiplied by the overall flare brightness.
Blur the vis mask by this radius.
Set the relative distance of the lightsource to the matte box, at which the flare will be invisible.

description.plain_text: Nuke supports Lens Flares by providing three different rendering operators: flares, sparkles and reflections. This operator creates flares that can be combined to create film or video camera lens flares. Flares are created by reflections between lenses in the multilayer lens setup inside a camera. Flares are generally round, oval, or roundish with 5 or 6 flattened sides. Due to different reflection and refraction coefficients based on wavelength, flares tend to show chroma shifting, generating rainbow-like outlines. Nuke Flares are implemented as a donut-like shape with a possibly filled center. Mmmm... donuts.... There are three radii: the outer radius is the outside of the donut, the middle radius is the thickest part, and the inner radius is where the donut hole would be. A flare defines two colors, the color of the donut itself, and the fill color for the donut 'hole'. If donut color and hole color are the same, flares will be rendered as disks.

This operator creates flares that can be combined to create film or video camera lens flares. Flares are created by reflections between lenses in the multilayer lens setup inside a camera. Flares are generally round, oval, or roundish with 5 or 6 flattened sides. Due to different reflection and refraction coefficients based on wavelength, flares tend to show chroma shifting, generating rainbow-like outlines.

Nuke Flares are implemented as a donut-like shape with a possibly filled center. Mmmm... donuts.... There are three radii: the outer radius is the outside of the donut, the middle radius is the thickest part, and the inner radius is where the donut hole would be.

A flare defines two colors, the color of the donut itself, and the fill color for the donut 'hole'. If donut color and hole color are the same, flares will be rendered as disks.
